questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to extend behavior without touching core logic, a common real-world requirement in polyglot stacks.

## Key Concepts
- Decorator/Interceptor pattern
- Runtime registries and resolution order
- Idempotent wrapping and error propagation

## Code Example
```javascript
interface DAO<T> { get(id:string): Promise<T> }
interface Decorator<T> { (dao: DAO<T>): DAO<T> }
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you handle decorator composition order and conflicts?
- How would you test the registry and wrapped DAOs with minimal mocks?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests the ability to design runtime extensibility with minimal core changes, using a Registry and Factory-like pattern alongside a clean Backend abstraction.

## Key Concepts
- Registry pattern for dynamic extension
- Strategy-like renderers decoupled from backends
- Backend adapters for SVG and Canvas

## Code Example
```javascript
interface Backend { begin(): void; draw(path: string): void; fill(): void; }
interface Renderer { render(shape: Shape, backend: Backend): void; }
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test adding a new renderer without rendering a full scene?
- How would you handle renderer lifecycle (initialization, disposal) in a long-running app?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design a small, extensible plugin system using runtime registries and the separation of concerns between formatting and sinking.

## Key Concepts
- Registry pattern for dynamic extensibility
- Strategy/Factory for pluggable formatters
- Async I/O and backpressure in sinks
- Graceful shutdown and error containment

## Code Example
```typescript
interface Formatter { format(msg: string, level: string): string; }
interface Sink { write(data: string): Promise<void>; }
class Registry {
  private formats = new Map<string, Formatter>();
  private sinks = new Map<string, Sink>();
  registerFormat(name: string, f: Formatter): void
  getFormat(name: string): Formatter
  registerSink(name: string, s: Sink): void
  getSink(name: string): Sink
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test runtime registration of new formats?
- How would you prevent a slow sink from blocking others?
